clue.text: An ancient tax, son, is quite the contrary!

parts.note: taken as written
a tithe was the tenth of produce once paid to the church
S is the standard abbreviation for son in family trees
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that an old levy on their boy is the very opposite of what they expected.
explanation.definitionFit: An antithesis is the direct opposite of something, exactly what 'quite the contrary' expresses.

clue.text: Mother up before doctor's round

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for mother is read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
MO is a medical officer, an army doctor

explanation.surface: Mum climbs the stairs before the GP comes calling on their rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Ammunition is counted in rounds, so a round is a single unit of the stuff.

clue.text: Suggestions must include name for such states of mind

indicators.note: the word for suggestions is made to take the abbreviation for name inside it

parts.note: traces are faint suggestions or hints of something

explanation.surface: A hypnotist's suggestions should mention the sort of mental states they induce.
explanation.definitionFit: Trances are dazed, hypnotic conditions of the mind, examples of the states the clue alludes to.

clue.text: Pull of the capital's museum?

parts.note: a famous London fortress now visited as a museum is read whimsically as a person who tows things, a puller belonging to the capital

explanation.surface: A question about what draws visitors to a city museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull' seems to mean attraction, but a tower is also one who tows, so London's tower becomes the capital's puller.
explanation.definitionFit: The great fortress on the Thames houses the Crown Jewels and is run as a museum in Britain's capital.

clue.text: Big birds seen eating dead parrots

indicators.note: the big birds take the word for dead inside, as if swallowing it

parts.note: emus are large flightless Australian birds
late means deceased, as in 'the late king'

explanation.surface: Large birds are spotted devouring dead parrots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parrots' looks like a noun for birds in the scene, but it is a verb: copies.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot someone is to repeat or imitate them, and to emulate is likewise to copy.

clue.text: Playwright's single book despatched unfinished

parts.note: I, the Roman numeral one, stands for a single

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for despatched is left off

parts.note: sent means despatched, as of a letter

explanation.surface: A dramatist's only manuscript is posted before it is complete.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist who wrote A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Trip curtailed over female vegan's food

indicators.note: the shortened trip goes over the letter for female, enclosing it
the last letter of the word for a trip is cut off, as a tail is docked

parts.note: a tour is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A woman's trip is cut short, and the talk turns to vegan cuisine.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUR loses its tail to give TOU, and 'over' wraps it round F.
explanation.definitionFit: Tofu, pressed soya bean curd, is a staple protein in plant-based diets.

clue.text: You bet regularly on employer being slower

indicators.note: every second letter of the words is taken in order

parts.note: one who employs something, uses it, so a user is an employer

explanation.surface: A gambler bets steadily on their boss being the less quick-witted one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slower' means slower on the uptake, not slower in speed.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtuse means dull-witted, so the comparative describes someone slower to understand.

clue.text: Assistant to worker accepting year is fundamental

indicators.note: the word for an assistant takes the year's abbreviation inside it

parts.note: an underling is a subordinate who serves under another worker

explanation.surface: A junior helper taking on a year's work is essential.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlying causes or principles are the basic, fundamental ones beneath the surface.

clue.text: Manx call for reversal of objective that hurt!

indicators.note: the word for objective is read backwards

parts.note: an aim is an objective or goal
ow is the cry one gives when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone yelps in pain on the Isle of Man after a plan goes backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Manx' is not about the Isle of Man: the Manx is a tailless breed of cat, so its call is a mew.
explanation.definitionFit: A Manx is a breed of cat, and a cat's cry is its mew.

clue.text: A foreign tourist attraction expected to lose heart without a view

parts.note: un is the French for a, so a foreign 'a'
a sight is something tourists go to see

indicators.note: the word expected loses all its inner letters, keeping only its first and last

explanation.surface: A foreign landmark that visitors were promised is a letdown, with nothing to look at.
explanation.walkthrough: In sport, a goalkeeper is unsighted when their view of the ball is blocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsighted means unable to see, deprived of a view by some obstruction.

clue.text: Where one may learn syntax is fashionable, they say?

parts.note: grammar covers the rules of syntax in a language

indicators.note: signals that the words for 'is fashionable' are spoken, giving a word that sounds like them

parts.note: 's cool, a contraction of is cool, means is fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone claims that studying sentence structure is trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cool' contracted to 's cool sounds like SCHOOL. A GRAMMAR SCHOOL is a selective British secondary school.
explanation.definitionFit: A school is a place where pupils go to be taught and to learn.

clue.text: One trapped in frantic rat race ruins precursor to main event

indicators.note: the numeral for one is caught inside the jumbled letters
frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in the frenzied rat race is ruined before the big moment arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' scrambles RAT RACE RUINS, and 'trapped in' puts I inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: A curtain-raiser is a short piece performed before the main play, hence any opening preliminary.

clue.text: A dangerous place for a matriarchy?

definitions.text: A dangerous place for a matriarchy?

parts.words: A dangerous place for a matriarchy?
parts.note: the perilous strip between front lines is read literally as territory ruled with men absent, as in a society run by women

explanation.surface: A question about where a female-led society would be at risk.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase for the deadly ground between opposing trenches is read as a land belonging to no man.
explanation.definitionFit: The deadly ground between enemy trenches is the classic perilous zone, and it literally has no man in charge.

clue.text: Work of side is rigidly set in ways

indicators.note: work as a verb, to knead or rework, tells us to rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: The team's tactics have become fixed and inflexible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' reworks the letters OF SIDE IS.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally turned to bone, figuratively it means hardened and inflexible in habits or views.

clue.text: Oily butters making a comeback, by Jove!

indicators.note: the word for butters is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: rams are animals that butt, so they are butters
my! is an exclamation of surprise like by Jove!

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims at how slick and greasy the butter spreads have become again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butters' is not dairy produce but things that butt: rams.
explanation.definitionFit: Oily, of a person's manner, means unctuously ingratiating, the same as smarmy.

clue.text: A legitimate target for blonde with grouse, say

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
grouse is an example of game birds that are hunted

explanation.surface: A fair-haired hunter with a bird shot is considered fair sport.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something open to attack or criticism is fair game, a permissible quarry.

clue.text: Presenter of a new group of singers missing one

indicators.note: the numeral for one is taken out of the word for the singers

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A host introduces a fresh vocal ensemble that is short of one member.
explanation.definitionFit: A news anchor is the main presenter who links a broadcast together.

clue.text: Record held by once ruined city on the continent

indicators.note: the word for record is held inside the other letters
ruined means wrecked, so the letters of the word once are rearranged

parts.note: a log is a written record, as in a ship's log

explanation.surface: Archives were kept by a city that was once left in ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once ruined' reads as history of the war-bombed city, but 'once' is the fodder and 'ruined' its anagram signal, making CONE for 'held by' to wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Cologne, Köln in German, is a major city on the Rhine in mainland Europe.

clue.text: Farm hands locking nonchalant male in study

indicators.note: the word for nonchalant and the male letter go inside the word for study

parts.note: a den is a private room for study
airy means casual and unconcerned

explanation.surface: Farm workers lock a casual man in the study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locking' just joins the definition to the wordplay; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dairymen are farm workers who look after cows and the milk they produce.

clue.text: Sucker pinching small brown horse

indicators.note: the word for a sucker grips the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a mug is a gullible person, a sucker
tan is a light brown colour

explanation.surface: A dupe steals a little brown horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pinching' looks like theft but tells MUG to hold S and TAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mustang is a wild or feral horse of the American West.

clue.text: Model reflects as stud, lacking answer, goes to pieces

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so the letters are moulded into a new form
the abbreviation for answer is dropped from the letters before they are shaped

explanation.surface: A model sees a stallion's reflection and falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes one A from REFLECTS AS STUD; 'Model' then rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that self-destructs destroys itself, falling to pieces of its own accord.

clue.text: Winter sportsman's captain very quietly disappearing

indicators.note: the musical marking for very quiet vanishes from the word for captain

parts.note: a skipper is the captain of a ship or team
pp, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quietly

explanation.surface: A team leader on the slopes quietly vanishes.
explanation.definitionFit: A skier is someone who skis, a typical winter sports participant.

clue.text: Thirty seconds? Time for a sweetie!

parts.note: thirty seconds is half a minute, and half the letters of minute give min

explanation.surface: After half a minute someone decides it is time for a sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the stretch: half a minute in time is also half the word MINUTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mint is a peppermint sweet, and a sweetie is British for a sweet or candy.

clue.text: Runs into spy in a part of the Americas

indicators.note: the letter for runs goes into the word for spy

parts.note: an agent is a spy
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone bumps into a secret agent somewhere in the New World.
explanation.definitionFit: Argentina is a country in South America, one portion of the Americas.

clue.text: Took a picture, capturing an example of African wildlife

indicators.note: the words hold the answer within their letters, as a camera captures an image

explanation.surface: A photographer snapped a shot of a wild animal on safari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capturing' seems to describe the photo, but it hides the letters in tOOK A PIcture.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a striped forest giraffe found only in the Congo, so a piece of African fauna.

clue.text: Positive response given to Germany's colours

parts.note: D is the international vehicle code for Germany
yes is an affirmative reply

explanation.surface: Germany says yes to its national flag colours.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyes are colouring agents, and colours can mean the pigments themselves.

clue.text: Common predicament, going topless gets the go-ahead

parts.note: a green is common land in a village, the village common

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for predicament is lost

parts.note: a plight is a predicament or difficult situation

explanation.surface: A common problem is solved when something gets approved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going topless' sounds racy but just removes the top letter. A village GREEN in Britain is a shared grassy common.
explanation.definitionFit: A green light signals permission to proceed, just as giving the go-ahead does.
